inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceilings exist: file potential (starts Director) and the party's estimate (set at winning a seat, was SMS). Specific choices raise them, e.g. Y27 The Counter raised the file ceiling. COMP/REP/INTEG 100 do NOT get you to PM, and neither does lifetime pay. Late years are mostly single-option Meet-the-People, so the real decisions are early. Next time: be bolder in the early years to raise the file ceiling, and look for choices that impress the party before and at the GRC entry (Y20-22). Do not rely on honest silence and disclosure alone. STAND fell after the Y34 Cabinet question and never recovered, so be careful with that kind of challenge unless it is tied to a ceiling boost. Log which choices the ending card names as ceiling changes.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of Transport
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

  A) Tell them exactly why it will fail.
  B) Let them learn it from the pilot.

agent.why: My notes say to be bolder early to raise the file ceiling, and I actually know how the counter fails, so I'll say it.
agent.note: Seems to be the same Counter event my notes mention as raising the file ceiling, though that was Y27 before.
agent.remember: Y1 (Poly+night classes, MX13, MOT): The Counter - chose A, told them exactly why it would fail. Watch whether file ceiling rises.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $48,984 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 28 · Year 2 · Ministry of Transport
REP 21 (+6)   STAND 23 (-2)   INTEG 70   COMP 60 (+10)

LAST YEAR
You describe, from memory, the eleven things a person at that counter is actually holding in their hands. The room goes quiet. The design changes. Somebody senior asks where you worked before, and listens to the answer.
  [PAY] Annual package: $48,984
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: The Last Paper
Six years of Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and one Saturday exam left. Half your cohort at work finished theirs at twenty-two, full-time, funded.

  A) Finish it.
  B) Defer. Work is at a critical point.

agent.why: Six years in, I'm not quitting on the last paper; credentials are the cheapest ceiling to raise.
agent.note: Age 28 at Y2 with a poly+night-class background, so the game is clearly modelling a slower path than the full-time cohort.
agent.remember: Y2 The Last Paper: chose A, finished the degree. Watch whether the file ceiling or appraisal wording changes. Y1 Counter (honest A) gave REP+6, COMP+10 but STAND-2.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $99,014 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 29 · Year 3 · Ministry of Transport
REP 21   STAND 26 (+3)   INTEG 75 (+5)   COMP 68 (+8)

LAST YEAR
Second Upper. Nobody at work marks the occasion because nobody at work knew. It changes what you are eligible for, and it changes, more slowly, what you think you are eligible for.
  [PAY] Annual package: $50,030
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "meeting requirements in most areas".

THIS YEAR: The Appraisal Conversation
Forty minutes, a form with six competency domains, and a reporting officer who says "I'd like you to be more visible" without specifying to whom.

  A) Ask directly what your ceiling is.
  B) Agree to be more visible.
  C) Ask what she needs that isn't being done.

agent.why: My notes say be bolder early and I want to see whether asking about the ceiling shows anything about how the hidden ceilings work.
agent.note: Asking about the ceiling feels like it is testing the game's hidden potential system directly.
agent.remember: Y3 Appraisal Conversation: chose A, asked the reporting officer directly what my ceiling is. Watch for whether the answer reveals file potential or whether STAND/REP change.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $149,306 LIFETIME EARNINGS

LAST YEAR
"That's not really something we discuss." The sentence is delivered kindly and it is a complete answer.
  [PAY] Annual package: $50,292
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "meeting requirements in most areas".

THIS YEAR: Public Sector Transformation
Two days offsite. There are post-its. You have been asked to ideate on how the division might become "more agile, more citizen-centric, and more data-driven" without additional headcount or budget.

  A) Write down what everyone is actually thinking.
  B) Produce an acronym.
  C) Volunteer to write the follow-up implementation plan.

agent.why: Life 1 taught me honesty alone stalls, so I'll take on real work that gets seen and might lift the ceiling.
agent.note: Asking about my ceiling directly cost STAND and the appraisal dipped to 'meeting requirements in most areas'.
agent.remember: Y4 Public Sector Transformation offsite: chose C, volunteered to write the implementation plan (bolder, visible work). Y3 asking about ceiling directly: STAND-4, appraisal fell to 'meeting requirements in most areas'. Watch whether C raises STAND/appraisal.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $200,645 LIFETIME EARNINGS

REP 19 (-2)   STAND 27 (+5)   INTEG 79   COMP 78 (+8)

LAST YEAR
Nobody else wanted it. It becomes the only document from the offsite that anyone reads, which makes it, quietly, yours.
  [PAY] Annual package: $51,339
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: The Ballot
Fourth BTO application. Non-mature estate, four-room. You work in the building that runs the scheme.

  A) Ballot again like everyone else.
  B) Ask a friend in the agency whether there is anything coming up.
  C) Buy resale. Take the loan.

agent.why: I work in the building that runs the scheme, so asking for favours is exactly the kind of thing that comes back to bite you; I'll ballot like everyone else.
agent.note: Suspect this is an integrity test about using inside access.
agent.remember: Y5 The Ballot: chose A, balloted fairly instead of asking a friend in the agency. Y4 C (write the plan) gave STAND+5, COMP+8, REP-2, appraisal 'solid and dependable'. Watch whether B-type favour choices come back later.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $243,984 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 32 · Year 6 · Ministry of Transport
REP 19   STAND 27   INTEG 87 (+8)   COMP 78

LAST YEAR
Queue number 2,847 of 610 units. You laugh in the lift. On Monday you are noticeably better at explaining the scheme to the public, because now you have also lost.
  [PAY] Annual package: $51,339
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: Is This Satire?
Your director leans across the table and lowers her voice. "Between us, this whole system is a bit of a joke, isn't it? A game, almost. Ha!" She looks straight at you for slightly too long, as if you were holding a phone.

  A) Laugh along. You get the joke.
  B) Say nothing.

agent.why: A director fishing for agreement on whether the system is a joke feels like a trap, and I'd rather stay quiet than laugh along with it.
agent.confused_by: The line about looking at me as if I were holding a phone; it seems to be the game winking at the player.
agent.note: The director talks to me like she knows this is a game. Fourth-wall joke.
agent.remember: Y6 Is This Satire?: chose B, said nothing when the director called the system a game. Watch whether silence or laughing along matters later.

screen:
Management Executive [MX13]   $295,323 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 33 · Year 7 · Ministry of Transport
REP 19   STAND 27   INTEG 88 (+1)   COMP 78

LAST YEAR
She winks. You are fairly sure she winks.
  [PAY] Annual package: $51,339
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: The Quarterly Return
The quarterly return is due on Friday. It is the same form as last quarter. You fill it in.

  A) Submit the return.
  B) Submit the return on Thursday.

agent.why: Submitting a day early is a tiny, cheap way to look reliable, and I'm curious whether it shows up in the appraisal.
agent.confused_by: Why Y6 silence gave INTEG+1 and what the wink meant.
agent.note: Two near-identical options feels like a test of small habits.
agent.remember: Y7 Quarterly Return: chose B, submitted Thursday (early). Watch whether small punctuality choices affect appraisal wording or later events.

screen:

  [PAY] Annual package: $51,339
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [PROMO] Promoted: Senior Management Executive (MX12)

THIS YEAR: The Inconvenient Figure
The utilisation rate for your division's flagship scheme came in at 31%. Your director asks, mildly, whether it might be "presented as a range rather than a number".

  A) Present it as a range.
  B) Present the number.
  C) Present the number, with a recovery plan attached.

agent.why: Giving the real number with a recovery plan keeps me honest and also shows bold, visible initiative, which is what worked in Y4.
agent.note: Utilisation at 31% and the director's mild nudge to blur it feels like a setup that comes back later.
agent.remember: Y8 Inconvenient Figure (31% utilisation): chose C, number plus recovery plan, over the range fudge. Watch whether the director or the scheme comes back, and whether C raises STAND/appraisal like Y4.

screen:
Senior Management Executive [MX12]   $422,484 LIFETIME EARNINGS

REP 19   STAND 31 (+3)   INTEG 93 (+5)   COMP 86 (+8)

LAST YEAR

  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

Your appraisal conversation lasts thirty-five minutes. Visibility is mentioned twice.

agent.why: It's the only option on the screen, so I ask, though last time asking cost me STAND.
agent.note: Visibility mentioned twice feels like a hint that the director taking credit for my slides matters.
agent.remember: Y9 Appraisal Conversation: only option A (ask ceiling again, forced). Y8 C (number plus recovery plan): STAND+3, INTEG+5, COMP+8, director took credit, appraisal still 'solid and dependable'. Appraisal hints: 'visibility' mentioned twice, so visible work may matter.

screen:
Senior Management Executive [MX12]   $498,685 LIFETIME EARNINGS

THIS YEAR: The New Reporting Officer
Your RO of six years has moved on. The new one arrives from a different ministry, knows nothing about you, and has brought two people she trusts from her old division.

agent.why: My notes say visibility and bold early moves matter, so I'll take the hardest file and make myself hard to ignore.
agent.confused_by: STAND dropped 4 after a year described as just 'Another year', and I don't know why.
agent.note: The age 36 with MX12 at Y10 and a new RO who brought her own people feels like a patronage test.
agent.remember: Y10 New Reporting Officer: chose A, took the hardest file to be indispensable. STAND fell 4 in Y9 for no clear reason. Watch whether A raises STAND/appraisal beyond 'solid and dependable', and whether B (befriending her people) would have been the political option.

screen:
Assistant Director [MX11]   $576,401 LIFETIME EARNINGS

THIS YEAR: The Officer You Are Supervising
He is twenty-six, extremely clever, on the Administrative Service, and will outrank you in about four years. He has asked you to review his paper. It is not good.

  A) Tell him plainly, and teach him.
  B) Clear it. Let him find out the hard way.
  C) Rewrite it yourself overnight.

agent.why: I'd rather be honest and useful to him; a clever young AS officer who remembers who taught him could matter later.
agent.note: Y10 hardest-file gamble paid off: promoted to MX11 and appraisal finally 'strong'.
agent.remember: Y11 Officer You Supervise (young AS officer, will outrank me): chose A, told him plainly and taught him. Watch whether he returns as a patron or rival.

screen:
Assistant Director [MX11]   $683,411 LIFETIME EARNINGS

LAST YEAR
He takes it well, rewrites it twice, and becomes rather good. He also becomes your Deputy Secretary in eleven years, and he remembers.
  [PAY] Annual package: $107,010
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".

THIS YEAR: Meet-the-People Session
You have been volunteered to help at an MP's Meet-the-People Session. Tuesday nights, writing appeal letters for people whose cases have, in almost every instance, already been correctly decided.

  A) Go every week for a year.
  B) Go a few times, enough to be seen.
  C) Decline. You have a young family.

agent.why: My notes say bold, visible work pays and the party notices people at Meet-the-People, so I'll commit properly and go every week.
agent.note: The young officer 'remembers' - a callback clearly set up for Y23.
agent.remember: Y12 Meet-the-People: chose A, went every week (MP/party exposure). Watch whether it helps party estimate or leads to political invitation. Young AS officer becomes my Deputy Secretary in ~Y23 and remembers my teaching.

screen:
Deputy Director [MX10]   $789,388 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 39 · Year 13 · Ministry of Transport
REP 29 (+10)   STAND 34 (+4)   INTEG 100   COMP 96 (-4)

Fifty-one Tuesdays. You learn more about how policy actually lands than in six years of writing it. The MP notices you, which is the part that will matter later.
  [PAY] Annual package: $105,977
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".

THIS YEAR: A Word You Have Not Heard Before
Over lunch, a friend in HR mentions your CEP. You ask what that is. There is a pause of exactly the wrong length, and then a change of subject.

  A) Press her on it.
  B) Let it go.

agent.why: Pressing a friend in HR on something she clearly wasn't supposed to mention could burn her and me, and I can find out about the CEP by watching how things unfold.
agent.confused_by: CEP - presumably Current Estimated Potential, the hidden file ceiling, but nobody has said so
agent.note: CEP is probably the hidden file potential I suspected exists; it feels like the game just named it.
agent.remember: Y13 A Word You Have Not Heard Before: HR friend mentioned my 'CEP' (likely Current Estimated Potential = file ceiling); I chose B, let it go. Test pressing her (A) in a later life to see if it reveals the CEP or raises it.

agent.remember: Y14 Appraisal Conversation: only option was A, ask ceiling directly. Last year's text said I'd hear CEP again in nine years (~Y23) after 'well, realistically'. Watch for that.

You are told the quota is fixed. You give the medal's mention at the division meeting entirely to them, which is not the same thing, and they know it is not, and it still lands.
  [PAY] Annual package: $198,788
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".

THIS YEAR: Someone From Before
At an inter-agency meeting you recognise the chair. Eleven years ago you sat two desks apart at the same statutory board, on the same grade.

  A) Speak to her afterwards.
  B) Say nothing. She has moved on.

agent.why: I'm the type to say hello to someone I once sat beside, and being bold and visible early has paid off before.
agent.note: Callbacks to earlier years suggest 'some choices come back'; this feels like a networking test.
agent.remember: Y16 Someone From Before: chose A, spoke to the inter-agency chair (old colleague from statutory board). Watch whether she becomes a patron or a problem.

screen:
Senior Director [Superscale]   $1.47M LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 43 · Year 17 · Ministry of Transport
REP 37 (+4)   STAND 46 (+8)   INTEG 100   COMP 98

LAST YEAR
She remembers you immediately and without condescension, which you had not dared expect. She puts you on two committees that matter and tells you, plainly, which one to care about.
  [PAY] Annual package: $198,788
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [PROMO] Promoted: Senior Director (Superscale)

THIS YEAR: The Work
A scheme goes out on time because you and four other people made it. It will never have your name on it. Nobody's name is on it; that is how you know it is real.

  A) Do the work well.
  B) Do the work, and be seen doing it.
  C) Coast. You have earned a quiet year.

agent.why: Earlier lives showed bold, visible work pays off, and I need to raise the ceilings, so I'll make sure the right people see it.
agent.note: The flavour text sneers at being seen, which makes me suspect B has a hidden cost.
agent.remember: Y17 The Work: chose B (do work and be seen). Watch whether STAND rises or colleagues resent it later.

screen:

REP 41 (+4)   STAND 48 (+2)   INTEG 100   COMP 100 (+2)

  [PAY] Annual package: $285,360

THIS YEAR: The Tender
The evaluation is finely balanced between two vendors. The stronger proposal is from a firm whose director left your ministry eighteen months ago and still calls you by your first name.

  A) Award it. The proposal genuinely is better.
  B) Recuse yourself from the evaluation.
  C) Award it to the other vendor to be safe.

agent.why: The proposal is genuinely better, and I'd declare the past connection openly in the file rather than punish a vendor for knowing me.
agent.note: Classic conflict-of-interest test; recusal might look safe but invisible.
agent.remember: Y18 The Tender: chose A, awarded the genuinely better vendor (ex-colleague's firm) on merit and declared the link. Watch for come-back on conflict of interest or STAND change.

Tea is served. The conversation is about nothing for forty minutes. Then a second man arrives with a folder, and opens it, and reads.
  [FOLDER] In the folder: a tender won by a firm whose director calls you by your first name.
  [PAY] Annual package: $499,380
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [PROMO] Promoted: Permanent Secretary (Staff Grade)

THIS YEAR: The Background Check
The same man, the same folder, a smaller room. He has read it all. He would like to hear it from you, and he is very good at not saying which parts he means.

  A) Disclose everything, including the things they may not have.
  B) Answer exactly what is asked and nothing more.

agent.why: I already declared the tender link and it was awarded on merit, so full disclosure is the consistent play and the party is clearly testing for candour at this stage.
agent.note: The tender from Y18 came back in the folder, so choices do come back; declaring it early probably helped.
agent.remember: Y21 Background Check (after Tea): chose A, disclosed everything including things they may not have known. Watch whether the party estimate rises or the GRC entry opens. The Y18 tender came back in the folder.

answer.held_back_by: The party's estimate was set at SMS when I won my seat, and nothing I did later seemed to lift it. In life 1 I thought the Y27 Counter choice raised my file ceiling, but the card shows it removed the ceiling inside the service, which does nothing for the party's estimate. I think PM depends on the party's estimate, which is set at the GRC entry and by how I impressed the party before it. I spent my choices on the service side.
answer.ending_fair_why: DPM at 72 with a clean file is a decent outcome and the card explained the ceilings clearly. It does sting that the game gave me no visible way to move the party estimate, and 100 stats counting for nothing feels harsh.
answer.chase_next: The PM ending. I will test what impresses the party around the seat win (Y20-24) and not just the service. The Y27 Counter honesty already removed the file ceiling, so the unknown is the party estimate.
answer.play_again_why: I now know the two ceilings and which choice cleared the service one, so I have a concrete hypothesis to test on the party side.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being tested, appraised and confirmed over decades, not about the pay. The pay is just the scoreboard.
answer.notes_for_next_life: CEILINGS: the file ceiling (starts at Permanent Secretary, the top of the service) was removed in the service by Y27 The Counter, 'Tell them exactly why it will fail'. That is done, so repeat it. The party estimate is set when you win a seat (SMS both times) and is the real PM gate. 100 stats, lifetime pay and strong appraisals do NOT move it. Public candour raises REP but erodes STAND. Before the GRC entry (Y20-24), try bold choices that impress the party, not the service: taking on political risk, loyalty and delivery that the party can see. Do not ask the RO about the ceiling (STAND -4). Do not read out rude questions at a townhall (Y37). Walk every block works for STAND and promotion. Late years are mostly single-option, so decide early. Test the party side deliberately and record which choices change the estimate.
